title: TypeScript Basic Types & Annotations
content: Annotate with `: type` after identifier. Primitives: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined`, `bigint`, `symbol`. Arrays: `string[]` or `Array<string>`. Tuples: `[string, number]`. `any` disables checking (avoid). `unknown` is safer — must narrow before use. `never` for unreachable code. Type alias: `type ID = string | number`.

title: Interfaces vs Type Aliases
content: Interface: `interface User { id: number; name: string; email?: string }`. Extend: `interface Admin extends User { role: string }`. Type alias: `type User = { id: number; name: string }`. Key differences: interfaces can be merged (declaration merging), type aliases can represent unions/intersections. Use `interface` for objects/classes, `type` for unions, intersections, and mapped types.

title: Generics
content: Generic function: `function identity<T>(arg: T): T { return arg; }`. Constrain: `function getLength<T extends { length: number }>(arg: T)`. Generic interface: `interface Box<T> { value: T }`. Built-in generic utilities: `Partial<T>` (all optional), `Required<T>`, `Readonly<T>`, `Record<K,V>`, `Pick<T,K>`, `Omit<T,K>`, `ReturnType<F>`, `Parameters<F>`.

title: Union & Intersection Types
content: Union `A | B`: value is either A or B. Narrow with `typeof`, `instanceof`, or a type guard. Intersection `A & B`: value has all properties of both. Discriminated union: add a literal tag field `kind: 'circle' | 'square'` to distinguish members in a switch. Use `in` operator to check property existence for narrowing.

title: Type Guards & Narrowing
content: User-defined type guard: `function isString(val: unknown): val is string { return typeof val === 'string'; }`. After `if (isString(x))`, TypeScript knows `x` is `string`. `instanceof` narrows class types. `in` narrows object shapes: `if ('name' in obj)`. Exhaustiveness check with `never`: `const _: never = val` in default branch of exhaustive switch.

title: Enums & Literal Types
content: Numeric enum: `enum Direction { Up, Down, Left, Right }`. String enum: `enum Status { Active = 'ACTIVE', Inactive = 'INACTIVE' }`. `const enum` is inlined at compile time (no runtime object). Alternative: use a string literal union `type Direction = 'Up' | 'Down' | 'Left' | 'Right'` — simpler and tree-shakeable.

title: Async/Await with Types
content: Async functions return `Promise<T>`: `async function fetchUser(id: number): Promise<User>`. Type the resolved value explicitly. For error handling, use `try/catch` with typed errors — catch blocks give `unknown`, so narrow with `instanceof Error`. Wrap with `Result<T,E>` pattern for explicit error typing without exceptions.

title: Mapped Types & keyof
content: `keyof T` produces a union of T's keys. Mapped type: `type Optional<T> = { [K in keyof T]?: T[K] }`. Add readonly: `{ readonly [K in keyof T]: T[K] }`. Template literal types: `type EventName<T extends string> = \`on${Capitalize<T>}\``. Conditional types: `T extends string ? 'yes' : 'no'`.

title: Classes & Access Modifiers
content: TypeScript classes add access modifiers: `public` (default), `private` (compile-time only), `protected`, `readonly`. Constructor shorthand: `constructor(private name: string, public age: number) {}`. Abstract class: `abstract class Shape { abstract area(): number; }`. Implement interface: `class Circle extends Shape implements Drawable { ... }`.

title: Decorators (Experimental)
content: Enable with `"experimentalDecorators": true` in tsconfig. Class decorator: `@sealed` applied before class definition. Method decorator: `@log` wraps a method. Property decorator for validation. Parameter decorator for DI. Used heavily in Angular and NestJS. Stage 3 native decorators (TC39) have slightly different semantics than TypeScript's legacy decorators.

title: tsconfig.json Key Options
content: `strict: true` enables all strict checks (recommended). `target`: output JS version (`ES2020`, `ESNext`). `module`: module system (`commonjs`, `esnext`). `paths`: path aliases `{ "@/*": ["./src/*"] }`. `noImplicitAny`: error on inferred `any`. `strictNullChecks`: `null`/`undefined` not assignable to other types. `outDir`: compiled output folder.

title: Built-in Utility Types
content: `Partial<T>` — all fields optional. `Required<T>` — all fields required. `Readonly<T>` — immutable. `Pick<T, 'a'|'b'>` — subset of fields. `Omit<T, 'password'>` — all except specified. `Record<string, number>` — dict type. `Extract<T, U>` — common members. `Exclude<T, U>` — remove members. `NonNullable<T>` — removes null/undefined.

title: Discriminated Unions (Pattern Matching)
content: Add a literal `type` or `kind` field to distinguish union members: `type Shape = { kind:'circle'; radius:number } | { kind:'square'; side:number }`. Then switch on `kind` — TypeScript narrows automatically. Add a default case with `const _exhaustive: never = shape` to catch unhandled cases at compile time.

title: Module Augmentation & Declaration Merging
content: Extend an existing module's types: `declare module 'express' { interface Request { user?: User } }`. Merge interfaces: two `interface Foo` declarations in the same or different files are merged. Global augmentation: `declare global { interface Window { analytics: Analytics } }`. Useful for adding types to third-party libraries without modifying their code.

title: Type Assertions & satisfies
content: Type assertion: `value as string` (compile-time cast, no runtime check). Non-null assertion: `el!.value` tells TS the value is non-null. `satisfies` operator (TS 4.9): `const config = { port: 3000 } satisfies Partial<Config>` — checks structure while preserving inferred literal types. Prefer `satisfies` over `as` when you need both validation and inference.

title: TypeScript Generics & Constraints
content: Generics parameterize types: `function identity<T>(arg: T): T { return arg; }`. Add constraints using `extends`: `function logLength<T extends { length: number }>(arg: T)`. Use `keyof` to lookup object keys: `function getProperty<T, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K) { return obj[key]; }`. This ensures type safety for dynamic access.

title: Conditional & Mapped Types
content: Conditional types choose types based on condition: `type IsString<T> = T extends string ? true : false`. Use `infer` to extract nested types: `type ReturnType<T> = T extends (...args: any[]) => infer R ? R : any`. Mapped types transform property keys: `type Readonly<T> = { readonly [P in keyof T]: T[P] }`. Use `-readonly` or `+?` to strip or add modifiers.
